summary: Adds a read-only checkpoint resume action router that classifies each persisted file path as already converged, repair committed staging, cleanup committed staging, materialize staged file, resume transfer, retry transfer, quarantine staging, or reject drift using durable SQLite rows and live filesystem/receipt evidence.
audit_findings: Rev0681 provided a safe executor for one terminal staging repair case, but callers still had to infer all other restart decisions from aggregate resume-view counters.
A restart path needs a typed per-path action plan before it should mutate pending materialization, partial transfer, cleanup, or quarantine state.
Partial staged files must not be treated as corruption merely because their full-file hash does not yet match; receipt coverage and action context must drive classification.
resume_action_checks: plan_sync_session_checkpoint_resume_actions loads the checkpoint resume view with durable and source proof by default while allowing destination and staging cleanliness to be advisory for classification.
The SQLite checkpoint database is opened read-only and must stay outside source, destination, and staging roots.
File plans join file results, apply intents, source manifest entries, source manifest chunks, and chunk receipt rows.
Stored absolute target and staging paths are checked against the caller's configured roots before an action is trusted.
Destination target bytes are checked against checkpointed source file size/hash for materialized rows.
Staged .part files are inspected as potentially partial evidence unless a terminal-clean row or complete receipt set makes a mismatch suspicious.
Receipt sidecars are verified by hashing their bytes back to persisted sync-chunk-receipt:v1 idempotency keys.
Missing chunks are returned for future transfer continuation.
Unexpected or tampered staging artifacts are classified as QuarantineStaging rather than repair or materialize actions.
